Dragging a Session clip to the User Library saves it as a Live Clip (Ableton/File/.alc), which keeps the clip settings and the track's instruments and effects. Useful for drum patterns with their kit, loop variations, and ideas set aside for later. See Ableton/Clip/How To/Save to Library.
The browser for finding and previewing sounds, devices, samples and presets, with search, filters, tags, collections and places.
The content pane lists the items in the selected label, or the results of a search or filter.
Name is always shown. Add more columns from the Content Options menu, also opened by right-clicking a column name, and drag column names to reorder them.
Click a column name to sort by it, ascending or descending. The Content Options menu also shows or hides file extensions.
Results match all the search terms, not any one of them: "electric bass" finds items with both words.
Cmd+F (Mac) / Ctrl+F (Win) jumps to the All label and puts the cursor in the search field.
Narrow results by clicking tags in the Filter View, or type # and a tag name, such as #Drums, with autocomplete.
The x button clears the search terms only; the Clear button in the Results bar also clears selected tags.
Keyboard-only flow: Cmd+F, type, down arrow into the results, arrows to move, Esc to clear and return to All.
4.2.1 Saving Search Results as Custom Labels
The Add Label button beside Clear saves the current results as a custom label in the Library.
4.2.1 Saving Search Results as Custom Labels
Tagging items with your own tags and saving the search makes a label that works like a Collection.
4.2.1 Saving Search Results as Custom Labels
Labels, factory or custom, can be renamed and given a new icon from their context menu; custom labels can be removed there too.
4.2.1 Saving Search Results as Custom Labels
The arrow buttons left of the search bar step back and forward through past searches and navigation.
Cmd+] / Cmd+[ (Mac) or Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[ (Win) go forward and back.
The Filter View lists filter groups and their tags for searching content by description.
Hide it with the Show/Hide Filter View toggle; the Filter View menu beside it picks which groups appear.
Click tags in a group to narrow the content pane; Cmd-click (Mac) / Ctrl-click (Win) selects several in one group.
Each label keeps its own set of visible groups and selected filters. Hide a group by right-clicking its name; "Reset Filter Groups to Default" in the Filter View menu brings the defaults back.
The Results bar counts the applied filters. Clear resets them and the search; Add Label saves the results.

Tags help find, organize and discover content. All factory content from the Core Library and bundled Packs carries descriptive tags; third-party Packs from the Ableton shop are tagged in the Sounds group.
Factory tags can't be removed, but you can add other tags, including your own, in the Tag Editor.

Background sound analysis auto-tags user samples up to 60 seconds long with the best-matching tag. Turn this off with Enable Auto Tags in the Filter View menu, or change or remove auto tags in the Tag Editor.
VST3 plug-ins get tags from their VST sub-category when it maps to one of Live's categories.
The Tag Editor, opened from the Filter View menu, shows and assigns tags for the selected item. Check or uncheck tags; Shift-select several items to tag them together.
Add Tag… adds a custom tag to any group; Add Group… at the bottom creates a new group, which appears in the Filter View once one of its tags is used, for example a group for field recordings.
Right-click a tag and choose Add Subtag in… to nest tags under a parent tag. The Creator group doesn't allow subtags.
Custom tags and groups can be renamed or deleted from their context menu; default groups and tags can't.
Quick Tags shows the selected item's tags. Add… assigns another, with autocomplete, or creates a new tag after a "Create new tag…" prompt, asking for its parent tag or group.
The X beside a tag you assigned removes it; factory tags stay.
With several items selected, it shows every tag on any of them and marks tags not shared by all with an asterisk.
